# Pinned strict JPEG decoder

`jpeg-js-0.4.4-strict.mjs` comes from npm `jpeg-js@0.4.4` `lib/decoder.js`, upstream canonical LF SHA256 `A3F175FD6F62D142AAD94D3BD90F3A30BE4E076BAF9B6A6FA31C8E84D9D4AA9F`. The repository/source is [jpeg-js](https://github.com/jpeg-js/jpeg-js/tree/v0.4.4). The npm archive integrity is retained in backend/package-lock.json. Canonical LF strict source SHA256 is `EF52562BD855357534059B441A93C935270D72C568DF5AB4CAE1E63EA581C0A0`.

Two reviewed changes: replace the CommonJS/window export with an ESM named export; replace the upstream scan-end skip loop with checks that unused alignment bits are all one and that the next bytes are a marker rather than unread entropy-tail payload. The exact jpeg-js0.4.4 encoder emits one stuffed all-one `FF00` alignment byte when its final MCU is already byte-aligned; only this inert byte is allowed once with zero residual bits, followed immediately by a marker. Repeated padding, arbitrary private payload and non-one alignment fail. No other decoder algorithm is changed. `community-jpeg` independently restricts framing/components/metadata/byte/dimension bounds, computes the real digest and actual decoded-pixel placeholder, and maps decoder failures to one fixed public error. Dev tests compare exact source provenance, equivalent valid pixels and concealed/corrupt entropy rejection. No runtime source rewriting or eval occurs.

The original Apache2.0 notice in the source is retained with `Apache-2.0-LICENSE.txt`; npm's Eugene Ware BSD redistribution license is retained as `jpeg-js-LICENSE.txt`. Both notices must accompany redistribution. Pinned npm jpeg-js remains a dev-only fixture encoder/reference, while the Edge imports this strict source. Actual native/browser format compatibility and hosted CPU remain acceptance gates. Rejecting explicit metadata/unread payload does not prove absence of information encoded through valid image pixels or steganography.
